title: Alexander the Great
summary: In little over a decade, Alexander of Macedon shattered the Persian Empire and carried Greek culture to the edge of India.

stories.title: Conquest of Persia
stories.summary: From the Granicus to the gates of Babylon, Alexander's army defeats every Persian force in its path.

events.title: Battle of the Granicus
events.body: Alexander crossed into Asia Minor and met a Persian satrap army on the banks of the Granicus River. A bold cavalry charge through the river broke the Persian line and opened the road into Anatolia.

events.title: Battle of Issus
events.body: Darius III assembled a massive army and marched to intercept Alexander in Syria. Fighting in a narrow coastal plain, the Macedonian phalanx crushed the Persian centre while Alexander drove toward the king's chariot, forcing Darius to flee.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.body: The island fortress of Tyre refused to surrender, so Alexander built a causeway across half a kilometre of sea and assaulted the walls with siege towers. After seven months the city fell, securing his control of the eastern Mediterranean.

events.title: Battle of Gaugamela
events.body: Darius gathered his last great army on the plain of Gaugamela in Mesopotamia. Alexander feigned a flank withdrawal, then punched through a gap in the Persian line and routed the entire force, leaving the empire defenceless.

events.title: Entry into Babylon
events.body: With Darius in flight, Babylon opened its gates to Alexander without a fight. The conqueror entered the ancient city in triumph and made it a capital of his new empire, adopting Persian court ceremony while claiming the mantle of the Great King.

stories.title: Indian Campaign
stories.summary: Alexander pushes east beyond Persia, crossing the Indus and fighting his last great battle on the Hydaspes.
